+assignees:

+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8e80'
+title: 'FoundationModels: remove the MLX buffer-pool override so MLXLanguageModel uses MLX''s default, as ChatSession does'
+---
+User decision 2026-10-31. `MLXLanguageModel` sets `Memory.cacheLimit` once per process: 256 MiB originally (f1573a93), then 1/32 of the working set (fadf1b16, ^1abqd92). Both are arbitrary. MLX's allocator defaults `max_pool_size_` to `block_limit_`, and ChatSession never overrides it. Per-round churn is 0.6–2 GiB and grows with context, so no constant fits.
+
+- [ ] Remove `configureGPUCacheOnce` and `gpuCacheLimitBytes(workingSetBytes:)` and their test (MLXLanguageModelGPUCacheLimitTests); an app can still set `Memory.cacheLimit` itself. Keep the GPU-built causal-mask positions.
+- [ ] Check the history for why 256 MiB was chosen; if a real constraint turns up (iOS, host-app budget), record it on the card and raise it with the user rather than silently dropping it.
+- [ ] Measure on the router path at 100k context: decode tok/s against the 1/32 limit, MLX active + cache memory, and peak process footprint.
+- [ ] Prove the pool yields under pressure: with target + drafter + flash + embedder loaded (Router's JointFit set) confirm MLX releases cached buffers instead of growing past the budget. Report the numbers so foundationmodelsrouter-ce can account for them.
+- [ ] Update the doc comments and any README mention.
+
+#mtp #foundation-models #perf
\ No newline at end of file

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m69pzrcnjv75famrfs6bn9nj
+  text: |-
+    Picked up. History check (`git log -S`, commit bodies, related cards):
+    - f1573a93 (#334, upstream FoundationModels drop) set 256 MiB with this rationale only: "Higher = less allocator thrash at the cost of slightly higher resident GPU memory. 256MB comfortably holds activations and KV cache for a 3B model without forcing pool evictions mid-forward-pass." It is a sizing for a 3B model that sets a floor against thrash. No iOS, jetsam or host-app budget constraint is recorded. 4cbef013 only named the constant; fadf1b16 made it 1/32 and its card ended "pending user confirmation of the process-wide pool size". The once-per-process static exists only so a consumer's own `Memory.cacheLimit` survives repeated loads, which removal satisfies trivially.
+    - mlx-swift's Memory.swift does say a smaller limit is "especially advantageous on devices with memory limits (e.g. iOS devices where jetsam limits apply)". That is a general upstream note, not a reason this repo recorded, and an app can still set `Memory.cacheLimit`. Flagged because MLXFoundationModels does build for iOS 27: with no override an iOS host gets MLX's default too, and it is the host's decision. Raising it in the final report.
+
+    Allocator facts (read, not yet proven): on a pool miss, if MLX active + cache + size >= gc_limit_ = min(0.95 x working set, block_limit_), it releases (required - gc_limit_) bytes from the LRU tail, or clears the pool when that is >= 90% of it. M5: gc_limit_ 73.9 GiB, block_limit_ 91.2 GiB. There is no OS memory-pressure handler in Cmlx, so memory outside MLX's own accounting does not trigger it. Buffers reuse only at near-exact size, so sizes that grow with context are not reused.
+    Router: budget() == recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize with no allowance; flash Qwen3-4B-4bit via loadModelContainer and embedder Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-4bit-DWQ via EmbedderModelFactory, all in one process and all on MLX's allocator, so gc_limit_ sits inside Router's budget.
+
+    Plan: the pressure proof runs FIRST, on the unmodified tree, because the removal depends on it. A temporary probe selects the arm in-process: before keeps the override, after fires the static then restores MLX's default, then one run on the real removed code validates that emulation.
